layouts.name: title
layouts.description: The cover of a deck: the deck title set large on the bottom line, a one-line subtitle, and who is presenting and when. Fill <Media> with a photo to give the cover an image that bleeds off the right edge; `picture: full` runs it across the whole slide, with the logo and text over it in white on dark scrims, for a photo with a calm lower left (sky, wall, road). `align: center` centres the logo, title and subtitle on a type-only cover, for a keynote or a short, bold title; with a photo the text stays on the left. Use it once, first; use section to open a part of the talk. Defaults to the gradient surface and hides the page chrome; the brand logo sits top left.

eyebrow.hint: Write a few words of at most 40 characters, for example `eyebrow: Budget committee`, or leave it out.

byline.hint: Name the presenter and team in at most 40 characters, for example `byline: Dana Okafor, Urban Forestry`.

date.hint: Write the date as the audience reads it, in at most 24 characters, for example `date: 18 November 2026`.

treatment.hint: Name one of the brand's image treatments, for example `treatment: plain` (every brand has it) to show a screenshot, map or chart in its own colors; `deck brand --json` lists them under imagery.treatments.

picture.hint: Write `picture: full` to run the <Media> photo across the whole slide behind the text, or leave it out to set it in the right five columns.

align.hint: Write `align: center` to centre the logo, title and subtitle on the slide, or leave it out to set them from the left.

chrome.hint: Write `chrome: false` to hide the page number, logo and progress bar on this slide, or `chrome: true` to show them.

body.description: The subtitle: one sentence that says what the deck is for. Set the deck title itself in `title:`.

media.description: A photo for the cover, as one with alt text; it fills the right five columns of the slide edge to edge, or the whole slide with `picture: full`, in the brand image treatment. Leave it out for a type-only cover.

layouts.name: section
layouts.description: A divider that opens a part of the talk: its number set large at the top, the part title on the bottom line and an optional one-sentence summary, whose two lines are kept free when it is left out so every divider sets its title at the same height. `numeral: large` makes the number a landmark: set in the surface tone, so large it runs off the bottom of the slide behind the title. `align: center` centres the number, title and summary on the slide. Fill <Media> with a photo for the part to fill the right five columns edge to edge; the text then stays on the left. Use one per part, in order, all on the same surface and with the same options, so the dividers read as a set. Defaults to the accent surface and hides the page chrome.

eyebrow.hint: Write a few words of at most 40 characters, for example `eyebrow: Budget committee`, or leave it out.

number.hint: Number the part, for example `number: 2` (shown as 02) or `number: IV`, in up to 3 characters.

numeral.hint: Write `numeral: large` to set the number as a large graphic behind the title, or leave it out for the number on the top line.

align.hint: Write `align: center` to centre the number, title and summary on the slide, or leave it out to set them from the left.

treatment.hint: Name one of the brand's image treatments, for example `treatment: plain` (every brand has it) to show a screenshot, map or chart in its own colors; `deck brand --json` lists them under imagery.treatments.

chrome.hint: Write `chrome: false` to hide the page number, logo and progress bar on this slide, or `chrome: true` to show them.

body.description: One sentence on what this part covers. Set the part title in `title:` (two to five words).

media.description: A photo for the part, as one with alt text; it fills the right five columns of the slide edge to edge, in the brand image treatment, and the text keeps to the left (`align: center` does not apply). Leave it out for a type-only divider.

layouts.name: statement
layouts.description: One sentence set large, on its own: the claim the talk turns on, or a quote. Up to three lines are set in the display style; a longer statement is set at quote size, in four lines at most, a little above the middle of the slide. Fill <Attribution> to set it as a quote with the speaker named below. Mark the two or three words that carry the claim with emphasis (`*front door*`) and write `emphasis: underline` to set them in the accent over a heavy rule, which reads on every surface. `align: center` centres a short statement on the slide, for a turn in the story or the ask. `size: giant` sets a statement of up to 5 words across most of the slide, larger than the display style, for the one line a keynote is remembered by. Use it sparingly, at most once per part. Defaults to the inverse surface; `title:` names the slide in the outline and is not shown.

eyebrow.hint: Write a few words of at most 40 characters, for example `eyebrow: Budget committee`, or leave it out.

emphasis.hint: Write `emphasis: underline` to set the words you mark with `*...*` in the accent over a heavy rule, or leave it out to set emphasis in italics.

align.hint: Write `align: center` to centre the statement and its attribution on the slide, or leave it out to set them from the left.

size.hint: Write `size: giant` to set a statement of up to 5 words across most of the slide, or leave it out.

chrome.hint: Write `chrome: false` to hide the page number, logo and progress bar on this slide, or `chrome: true` to show them.

body.description: The statement: one sentence, or two short ones, no list. For a quote, write the words without quotation marks; the layout sets them. With `emphasis:`, mark the words that carry the claim, once: `Identity is now your *front door*`.

attribution.description: Who said it: the name, then their role, for example "Dr. Amaka Bello, public health officer". Makes the statement a quote.

variants.name: `size: giant`; leave `size` out for a longer statement

layouts.name: content
layouts.description: A title that states the point, then a short paragraph, up to six bullets, or a sentence and bullets. Fill <Aside> with a key fact or definition to set it in a column beside the text. Sparse text is set larger and placed in the middle of the space; `width: full` runs the body across all twelve columns for a table, chart or component. The workhorse for explaining one idea; use split when the point needs a picture beside it, and stats when it rests on numbers.

eyebrow.hint: Write a few words of at most 40 characters, for example `eyebrow: Budget committee`, or leave it out.

width.hint: Write `width: full` to run the body across all twelve columns (a table, a chart or a component), or leave it out for the eight-column reading measure.

chrome.hint: Write `chrome: false` to hide the page number, logo and progress bar on this slide, or `chrome: true` to show them.

body.description: A paragraph, up to six bullets, or one sentence followed by bullets; with `width: full`, a table, chart or component. Set the takeaway in `title:`. Wrap points in <Step at={n}> to reveal them in turn.

aside.description: A key fact, definition or callout beside the body: a short ### heading and a sentence or two.

footnote.description: A source or caveat on the bottom line, in a sentence or two.

layouts.name: split
layouts.description: Text beside a picture or the evidence for it: a title and a short paragraph or bullets on one side, a photo, chart, diagram, table or component on the other. `ratio` shares the columns (text:media, 1:1, 5:7 or 7:5), `side` puts the media left or right, and `bleed: true` runs a photo to the edges of the slide. Photos fill the frame in the brand image treatment; other media is centred in it and can fill it with `height: 100%`. Use content when there is nothing to show.

eyebrow.hint: Write a few words of at most 40 characters, for example `eyebrow: Budget committee`, or leave it out.

ratio.hint: Share the columns text:media with `ratio: 1:1`, `ratio: 5:7` (wider media) or `7:5`.

side.hint: Put the media on the `left` or the `right` (the default).

bleed.hint: Write `bleed: true` to run a photo to the slide edges, or leave it out to frame it.

treatment.hint: Name one of the brand's image treatments, for example `treatment: plain` (every brand has it) to show a screenshot, map or chart in its own colors; `deck brand --json` lists them under imagery.treatments.

chrome.hint: Write `chrome: false` to hide the page number, logo and progress bar on this slide, or `chrome: true` to show them.

body.description: The text side: a short paragraph, up to four bullets, or a sentence and bullets. Set the takeaway in `title:`. The 5:7 column holds about 30 words.

media.description: What the text points at: one with alt text (imported from the deck's assets/ or served from its public/ folder), a chart, diagram, table or component. Photos fill the frame and are cropped to it; anything else is centred and may fill it with `height: 100%` (the frame is a size container, so `100cqh` works too).

caption.description: A caption or credit for the media, in a short sentence.

footnote.description: A source or caveat on the bottom line of the text side.

layouts.name: stats
layouts.description: Two to four big numbers in a row, each with what it counts and, optionally, how it changed. The title states what the numbers mean together. The row stands on one line on every stats slide; set `highlight: true` on the stat the point rests on. Use it when the point is the size of something; use a chart (or split with one) for a trend, and a table for more than four figures; use market for nested sizes or dashboard for related charts.

eyebrow.hint: Write a few words of at most 40 characters, for example `eyebrow: Budget committee`, or leave it out.

stats.hint: List 2 to 4 stats, each with `value` (as shown, such as "34%", up to 8 characters), `label` (up to 48 characters, 32 in a row of four), and optionally `delta` ("+12% since 2023", up to 24 characters), `tone` (positive, negative or neutral; set it when a fall is good news), `trend` (up, down or flat, for a delta without a sign) and `highlight: true` for the stat that matters most.

chrome.hint: Write `chrome: false` to hide the page number, logo and progress bar on this slide, or `chrome: true` to show them.

body.description: One sentence of context under the title. Set what the numbers mean together in `title:`.

footnote.description: The source of the numbers, on the bottom line.

layouts.name: equation
layouts.description: A number built from its parts, written as a sum: two to four figures (`terms:`) in a row, each with a label and joined to the one before by an operator (`op: times`, `plus`, `minus` or `divide`, set as ×, +, −, ÷), then an equals sign and the `result:` set largest on an accent panel that runs to the right and bottom edges of the slide. The figures share a baseline and the operators are set quieter than the figures; `reveal: true` brings the terms in left to right, one per step, and the result last, counting up. Use it for a bottom-up market size (customers × price × frequency), a business model (bookings × take rate = revenue) or unit economics (lifetime value ÷ acquisition cost); use stats when the figures stand side by side without adding up, and a chart for a trend; use market for nested market sizes.

eyebrow.hint: Write a few words of at most 40 characters, for example `eyebrow: Budget committee`, or leave it out.

terms.hint: List 2 to 4 terms in the order the sum reads, each with `value` (the figure as shown, such as "2,400" or "$380", up to 8 characters) and `label` (what it counts, up to 32). Every term after the first takes `op`, the operator before it: times, plus, minus, divide.

result.hint: Write `result:` with `value` (the figure the terms come to, up to 8 characters, such as "$1.1M") and `label` (what it is, up to 40 characters).

reveal.hint: Write `reveal: true` to bring the terms in one per step, left to right, and the result on the last step, or leave it out to show the whole equation at once.

chrome.hint: Write `chrome: false` to hide the page number, logo and progress bar on this slide, or `chrome: true` to show them.

body.description: One sentence under the title on what the result means. Put the figures in `terms:` and `result:`, not here.

footnote.description: The source of the figures, on the bottom line under the terms.

layouts.name: market
layouts.description: Two or three nested market sizes from `sizes:`, outermost first, each with a label, a figure and a one-line note. Bottom-aligned nested circles on the left encode the figures by area; label, figure and note stack consistently beside them. The innermost circle and figure, the part you can win, carry the accent. Very small circles keep a minimum visible diameter, a labelled share of their parent, and an explicit "Marker enlarged" disclosure. `labels.share` and `labels.minimum` override that wording. Close or equal scopes, and figures that cannot determine an exact area, use a typographic ladder instead. `reveal: true` introduces each size from the outside in. Use it to distinguish total, serviceable and obtainable demand, or a whole market and a reachable segment. Use equation when the audience needs to check the market arithmetic, stats for independent figures without nesting, and a chart for a longer quantitative series.

eyebrow.hint: Write a few words of at most 40 characters, for example `eyebrow: Budget committee`, or leave it out.

sizes.hint: List 2 to 3 sizes, outermost first, each with `label` (up to 20 characters), `value` (a number or a figure as shown, up to 8 characters including prefix and suffix, such as "€3.0B") and `note` (one line, up to 40 characters). For proportional circles use exact positive figures in the same currency or unit, largest first; compact magnitudes k, M, B and T and comma thousands separators are supported. The last size is the part you can win. Circle areas are proportional, with a labelled minimum for very small values. Close or equal scopes and other figure formats use a typographic ladder.

labels.hint: Optional share and minimum labels, each up to 24 characters. `share` defaults to "{share} of {parent}"; keep those placeholders for the exact percentage and enclosing figure. `minimum` defaults to "Marker enlarged" and discloses a circle held above its proportional size for visibility.

reveal.hint: Write `reveal: true` to show the items one per step, in order, or leave it out to show them all at once.

chrome.hint: Write `chrome: false` to hide the page number, logo and progress bar on this slide, or `chrome: true` to show them.

body.description: One sentence under the title defining the market or its common unit.

footnote.description: The source, date or qualification of the market figures, on the bottom line.

layouts.name: dashboard
layouts.description: Two to four small charts or number components under one takeaway title: two side by side, three in a row, or four in a two-by-two grid. List each short heading in `panels:` and put one kit chart or number component per panel in the body, in that order. Each panel's title names the measure, unit and period. With four panels, use at most two plotted charts; fill the other panels with BigNumber, Progress or Sparkline. With three or four panels omit chart captions, and keep a unit or percent/currency format on every chart. In three or four panels keep area and line chart units short or put the full unit in the panel heading. Highlight the same subject in every panel (as `highlight="2026"` in both charts), or only in the panel the title is about. Put shared sources in <Footnote>. `reveal: true` keeps headings and rules visible and reveals one plot per step; the shared source stays visible throughout. A Table may have up to four data rows and three columns, in two panels only. Use chart for one detailed plot or a chart with an aside; if every panel is a number, use stats. Use separate slides for different conclusions.

eyebrow.hint: Write a few words of at most 40 characters, for example `eyebrow: Budget committee`, or leave it out.

panels.hint: List 2 to 4 panels, each with a `title` of up to 24 characters (18 with three or four panels). Each title names the measure, unit and period. Write one direct component per heading. With four panels use at most two plotted charts and BigNumber, Progress or Sparkline for the rest.

data.hint: List datasets by name, each a list of rows, and name one from a chart with `data="name"`: `data: { regions: [{ region: EMEA, revenue: 4.2 }] }`. Inline rows (data={[...]}) and imported JSON or CSV files work too.

reveal.hint: Write `reveal: true` to show the items one per step, in order, or leave it out to show them all at once. Headings and rules stay visible; only plots reveal, with the source always visible.

chrome.hint: Write `chrome: false` to hide the page number, logo and progress bar on this slide, or `chrome: true` to show them.

body.description: Exactly one direct kit chart or number component per panel, in heading order. Each panel's title names the measure, unit and period. Use one series and at most four categories with labels up to 11 characters in two panels; with three or four panels use at most three categories and seven-character labels. LineChart and AreaChart x labels are periods of up to four characters (Mar, Q3, 2026). With three or four panels keep area and line chart units short or put the full unit in the panel heading; with three panels keep the largest value to nine characters including the unit (800 trees, 1.5K), using K or M for thousands. With four panels allow at most two plotted charts (BarChart, LineChart, AreaChart, Donut and similar); use BigNumber, Progress or Sparkline in the remaining panels. With two or four panels set Donut center="none"; keep shares and labels outside the ring. A Sparkline belongs beside numbers, not as a panel's only plot. Keep number values to eight characters and number labels to 18 characters with three or four panels. Omit captions with three or four panels; in two panels captions may use up to 32 characters.
